active_paradigms.idea: Binary search on the answer with a feasibility check via bin-packing-style assignment
active_paradigms.description: Instead of greedily constructing a placement, binary search on the target maximum KVPR value T. For a candidate T, run a feasibility check: assign models to GPUs one by one (ordered by decreasing req_rate/slo) using a first-fit / best-fit rule where a model m can go on GPU g only if (load_g + r_m)/(free_g - size_m) <= T and free_g > size_m, preferring the GPU with least remaining free memory that still fits (to preserve large free blocks). If all models are placed, T is feasible; binary search downward. This directly optimizes the min-max objective rather than relying on greedy orderings that only indirectly target it. Use ~40 iterations of bisection between 0 and a crude upper bound from the current greedy. Keep the local-search refine as a final polish on the best feasible placement.
active_paradigms.cautions: Feasibility check must handle models that fit nowhere under T (return infeasible, not error). Use tolerance ~1e-9 in bisection. If even T=inf fails (memory infeasible), fall back to best-effort placement. First-fit ordering by size descending helps feasibility.
active_paradigms.approach_type: custom binary search with bin-packing feasibility

active_paradigms.idea: Simulated annealing over model-to-GPU assignments with a penalized objective
active_paradigms.description: Represent the placement as an array mapping each model index to a GPU. Start from the best greedy solution. Run simulated annealing: at each step pick a random model and either move it to a random GPU or swap it with a random model on another GPU. Score a state by max KVPR across GPUs plus a large penalty * (memory overflow amount) so infeasible states are allowed transiently but strongly discouraged, enabling the search to pass through infeasible intermediate states that greedy/local search cannot. Use a geometric cooling schedule (e.g., T from 1.0 down to 1e-4 over ~20000 iterations) with the standard Metropolis acceptance. Keep the best feasible state ever seen. This escapes the local optima that the current steepest-descent local search gets stuck in.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: primary evaluator score via better global exploration of the assignment space
active_paradigms.cautions: Cache load[] and free[] arrays incrementally on each move for O(1) max recomputation (only two GPUs change). Ensure the returned placement is always feasible (memory fits); track best-feasible separately. Use a fixed seed for determinism. Watch runtime limits — cap iterations adaptively to model count.

active_paradigms.idea: Continuous relaxation solved with scipy.optimize.minimize (SLSQP) followed by rounding
active_paradigms.description: Relax the discrete assignment: let x[i][g] in [0,1] be the fraction of model i assigned to GPU g. Formulate a continuous minimax program: minimize T subject to for each GPU g: sum_i x[i][g]*r_i <= T*(80 - sum_i x[i][g]*s_i) with the free-memory term kept positive, sum_g x[i][g] = 1, and 0 <= x <= 1. Solve with scipy.optimize.minimize using SLSQP or trust-constr from several starting points (e.g., uniform assignment and greedy solutions). The fractional solution reveals which models are split across GPU boundaries — models with x near 0 or 1 are confidently assigned; split models get resolved by a small local search. This gives a global lower bound and a well-guided starting point the greedy cannot reach.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: primary evaluator score via a global continuous lower bound and informed initialization
active_paradigms.cautions: The KVPR constraint is bilinear (T times free memory); linearize by fixing free memory from the previous iterate or substitute variable f_g = 80 - sum x s and iterate. Guard against free memory approaching zero (add margin). Handle SLSQP failures gracefully by falling back to the greedy result. Round only models with fractional mass and verify feasibility after rounding.
